nodes.description: The realised malformation is confined to the apical digital structures: hypoplasia or absence of distal phalanges with absent or dystrophic nails, typically in more than half the digits of both hands and feet, and thumbs that may appear digitalized. Because the terminal phalanx and the nail unit develop together, the anonychia is part of the same apical lesion rather than a separate ectodermal defect. Nothing outside the autopod is affected — no short stature, no developmental delay, no other skeletal abnormality, and none of the Andersen-Tawil phenotype that KCNJ2 coding mutations produce.

nodes.description: Boundary-crossing duplications at 17q24.3 copy KCNJ2 and neighboring noncoding regulatory sequence. The original Cooks duplications also include KCNJ16. Their regulatory consequence depends on the extent of the duplicated interval. In the experimental mouse series, duplicating Kcnj2 and Kcnj16 within their original TAD did not produce the digit phenotype, whereas incorporation of Kcnj2 into a neo-TAD with Sox9 regulatory sequence did. This distinguishes the pathogenic regulatory rearrangement from gene copy-number gain alone.

nodes.description: Whole-mount in situ hybridization in Dup-C mice shows Kcnj2 expression in the digit anlagen with a Sox9-like spatial pattern. Limb-bud RNA-seq at E12.5 and E17.5 also shows increased Kcnj2 expression, while Sox9 and Kcnj16 remain unchanged. The spatially ectopic expression supports GOE; the quantitative increase alone would not. A Dup-C2 allele including Kcnj2 but not Kcnj16 also produces the digit phenotype. These are model measurements, not direct expression measurements from human embryonic digits, and they do not demonstrate altered intrinsic channel activity.

nodes.description: The duplicated KCNJ2 gene occupies the neo-TAD together with part of the SOX9 regulatory landscape. Capture Hi-C and 4C-seq in engineered Dup-C mouse limb buds demonstrate new contacts within this domain; patient fibroblast 4C-seq also demonstrates ectopic KCNJ2 contacts with the duplicated SOX9 regulatory region. SOX9 itself remains outside the duplication. A gene-free neo-TAD in the Dup-L control is phenotypically silent, so domain formation alone is insufficient for the limb phenotype. The contact measurements are distinct from the expression assays below.

nodes.description: Approximately 2.02 Mb duplication represented in POSTRE Table 1 patient Nr3 and Supplementary Data 3 as hg19 chr17:68020547-70038208, attributed there to the Cooks syndrome patient in Franke et al. (2016). These are POSTRE-reported interval bounds, not independently verified nucleotide-resolved junctions or a newly identified patient. The interval contains KCNJ2 and KCNJ16 coding sequence and intergenic regulatory sequence 5' of SOX9, while sparing SOX9 itself. KCNJ2 is both physically duplicated and the regulatory target. The pathogenic model is enhancer adoption within a neo-TAD, supported by patient-fibroblast chromatin contacts and corresponding engineered mouse alleles with ectopic digit expression. The GOE assignment uses the mouse spatial-expression evidence; it is not a claim that POSTRE experimentally measured this patient's expression.
